title: Set Financial Goals
concept: A financial goal turns a general wish into a measurable plan by defining an amount, deadline, monthly contribution, and priority.
learningObjective: Learn how to turn a vague financial wish into a measurable goal with a target amount, deadline, priority, and contribution plan.
primaryMisconception: Motivation alone is enough to reach a financial goal.
secondaryMisconceptions: A goal does not need a specific amount or deadline.
All financial goals should receive the same priority.
keyTakeaway: A financial goal needs an amount, deadline, and contribution plan.

screens.title: “Save More” Means What?
screens.content: “I want to save more” sounds good. But how much, by when, and which goal should receive your limited money first?
screens.illustration: Four goal cards—laptop, emergency fund, trip, and education—surround a vague Save More note.

screens.title: Four Goals, One Budget
screens.content: After essential expenses, you can save Rs. 25,000 monthly. You want a laptop, emergency fund, trip, and further education.
screens.illustration: A Rs. 25,000 monthly savings meter appears beside four empty goal cards.

screens.title: The First Draft
screens.content: Your first plan requires Rs. 35,000 monthly. It funds every goal quickly, but it exceeds your available savings by Rs. 10,000.
screens.illustration: The monthly plan fills beyond the Rs. 25,000 limit and displays a Rs. 10,000 shortfall.

screens.title: Something Must Change
screens.content: You can change deadlines, contributions, amounts, or priorities. Motivation cannot make an unaffordable plan fit the budget.
screens.illustration: Four adjustable controls appear beside the over-budget plan.

screens.title: Which Goal Can Be Measured?
screens.question: Which statement is the clearest financial goal?

options.response: This shows intention, but it does not define an amount, deadline, or contribution plan.

options.text: I will try harder next month
options.response: Effort may help, but progress cannot be measured without specific numbers and timing.

options.text: Save Rs. 120,000 in 12 months by contributing Rs. 10,000 monthly
options.response: Correct. The amount, deadline, and monthly action are clearly defined.
The goals still need separate amounts, deadlines, contributions, and priorities.

screens.title: Turn Wishes Into Plans
screens.instruction: Set an amount, deadline, monthly contribution, and priority for each goal. Keep the total within your Rs. 25,000 monthly savings budget.

protectedEssentialExpenses.description: Rent, bills, food, debt payments, and other essentials are already covered and cannot be reduced inside this activity.

educationalAssumptions: The learner has Rs. 25,000 available monthly after essential expenses.
All goals and amounts are fictional examples.
No interest or investment returns are included.
Prices remain unchanged during the activity.
A goal is funded when monthly contribution multiplied by deadline equals or exceeds the goal amount.
Actual costs, income, and priorities may change.
Adjusting a goal is not failure.
The activity does not provide personalised financial advice.

startingPlan.feedback: Each goal is measurable individually, but the combined plan exceeds the available monthly savings.

priorityRules: High-priority goals should be funded before lower-priority goals receive optional extra contributions.
A high priority does not guarantee immediate completion.
More than one goal may be high priority.
A low-priority goal may receive a smaller contribution, longer deadline, or temporary pause.
The builder does not force one universal priority order.

exampleValidCompletion.feedback: Every goal remains measurable and funded. Lower-priority deadlines were extended so the plan fits the budget.

firstDecisionCheck.question: The plan needs Rs. 35,000, but only Rs. 25,000 is available. What must happen?

options.text: At least one amount, deadline, contribution, or priority must change

firstDecisionCheck.explanation: The plan must fit the money available. Motivation cannot remove a Rs. 10,000 shortfall.

options.text: Continue the Rs. 25,000 plan and ignore the shortfall
Review contributions, deadlines, amounts, and priorities

validationRules: All four goals must be reviewed.
Every active goal must have an amount above zero.
Every active goal must have a deadline between 3 and 60 months.
Every active goal must have a priority.
Monthly contribution multiplied by deadline must meet or exceed the goal amount.
Total monthly contributions must not exceed Rs. 25,000.
All high-priority goals must be on track.
Both interaction questions must be answered correctly.

scoringRules.label: Complete and Prioritised
conditions: All active goals are on track.
Monthly total is Rs. 25,000 or less.

scoringRules.label: Affordable but Needs Review
conditions: One lower-priority goal is underfunded or paused without a revised deadline.

config.validationMethod: Check all goal fields, funding calculations, total monthly contributions, priority rules, and both decision questions.
config.retryBehavior: Keep valid goal settings. Highlight only underfunded, undefined, over-budget, or poorly prioritised goals.

accessibilityAlternative.method: Present each goal as a form with amount, deadline, contribution, and priority controls. Provide Previous Goal and Next Goal buttons.
accessibilityAlternative.screenReaderInstruction: Set the amount, deadline, monthly contribution, and priority for each goal. Listen to the funding status and remaining balance.

feedback.success: Goal plan complete! You turned four wishes into measurable actions that fit one monthly savings budget.
feedback.incorrect: Check the amount, deadline, monthly contribution, and priority for each goal. Then compare the total with Rs. 25,000.
feedback.incomplete: Complete every active goal and answer both planning questions before finishing.

screens.title: A Wish Becomes a Plan
screens.content: You turned general wishes into financial goals by adding amounts, deadlines, monthly contributions, and priorities. These details make progress measurable and reveal whether the complete plan fits your budget. Motivation can help you begin, but it cannot replace the required monthly action. Goals may also need adjustment when income, expenses, prices, or priorities change. Revising a plan is not failure—it is how the plan stays realistic.
screens.simpleSummary: Define the target, deadline, monthly action, and priority.
screens.illustration: A vague wish card transforms into a goal card containing amount, deadline, monthly contribution, and priority.

screens.title: Replacing a Motorbike
screens.content: Danish wants to replace his motorbike in two years. He estimates a Rs. 300,000 target and calculates a Rs. 12,500 monthly contribution. When his rent increases, he extends the deadline instead of abandoning the goal.
screens.illustration: A motorbike goal card changes from 24 months to a longer deadline after a rent increase.

reviewChecklist.notes: The mission focuses on turning vague financial wishes into measurable goals.
The mission connects amounts, deadlines, contributions, priorities, and budget limits using transparent calculations.
The mission uses adult savings, emergency funds, education, travel, laptops, essential expenses, rent changes, and limited income.
The mission teaches financial goal planning and does not recommend investments or financial products.
No investment returns are used in the goal calculations.
The mission does not discuss stocks or market prices.
Low-priority goals, paused goals, limited budgets, and revised deadlines are presented without judgement.
The mission states that income, expenses, prices, priorities, and personal circumstances may change.
The mission uses PKR, monthly savings, education, emergency expenses, laptops, trips, rent, and common adult financial decisions in Pakistan.
The learner defines and balances amounts, deadlines, monthly contributions, and priorities for four goals.
The quiz addresses vague goals, motivation-only plans, underfunded targets, and measurable actions.

reviewChecklist.item: Mission can be completed in under five minutes
reviewChecklist.notes: The learner reviews four goal cards, adjusts a small set of fields, answers two interaction checks, and completes three quiz questions.

reviewChecklist.item: Language matches the target reading level
reviewChecklist.notes: The language is practical, clear, respectful, and suitable for beginner adults.
